name: Question headline cards
looks: On a flat accent-colour card, a two-line question headline sits over a huge ghost punctuation mark watermarked behind it, with a single emoji-style icon and a thin progress dash rail underneath marking position in a sequence. The card cuts to a near-identical one with new copy and a new icon, same layout, same rhythm, then whip-pans into the next section.
build: Static card per question, hard cut on the beat; the headline is two text rows with a shared baseline grid, the ghost watermark a single oversized glyph at ~15% opacity behind the type. The progress rail is a row of short dashes with the active one filled solid; it advances one dash per card. The whip-pan out is a fast horizontal blur-scale (1x to 1.4x in under 0.15s) into the next scene's hard cut.
sound: A dry tick on each card's arrival, a short whoosh under the whip-pan.
prompt: Ask the viewer a short, punchy question on a flat colour card, a huge ghost punctuation mark behind the type for scale, with a small icon underneath standing in for the topic. Cut to a near-identical card with a new question and icon, same rhythm, and track position with a thin progress rail so the pair reads as a short set.
